title: onboard-solaris-13b-v1.0-perf-metadata-changelog-automation
author: Aisha Khan
description: Onboard Solaris-13B v1.0 to the model registry with performance profiles, metadata, and automated changelog/release-notes generation. Motivation: Solaris is an open 13B variant that provides competitive latency/quality for our mid-tier inference offering. This PR adds model metadata (model card, tokenizer/architecture tags, supported quantization formats), generates initial perf profiles for supported instance types (g4dn, a10g, p4d-lite), and wires the changelog automation so new model onboardings produce a draft release note in the registry UI and trigger the release-notes pipeline. Checklist: [x] model metadata & model card added [x] perf benchmarks added and validated [x] changelog automation hook implemented [x] unit tests & validations [x] docs updated. Links: model artifact storage: s3://redwood-models/solaris/13b/v1.0, linear: ENG-3245. Notes: perf numbers were collected with the latest runtime image and include both cold and warm KV-cache scenarios. This is squashed into a single merge commit and includes a follow-up job to publish the release note to the docs site.

release_notes: - Onboard Solaris-13B v1.0: initial release with model card and performance profiles. - Supported quantization: fp16, int8, q4_0 with recommended q4_0 profile for latency-sensitive workloads. - Performance profiles included for g4dn, a10g, and p4d-lite instance types. - Changelog and release-notes automation: a draft release note is generated automatically and published to the docs pipeline.
changelog_automation_details: Added scripts/changelog/generate_release_note.py which consumes metadata.json and perf profiles to render a release note using templates; wired into ci/pipeline/release-notes.yml so model-onboard PRs produce a draft artifact and optional publish step. The automation uses a tags-based trigger (label 'release-notes') and validates the presence of model_card.md and perf profiles before generating the draft.
notes: Perf numbers represent median latency and tokens/sec across 100 warm runs with batch sizes 1 and 8. See perf/profiles YAMLs for exact numbers. No breaking API changes. Follow-up work: automate per-region model routing metadata and add Dedicated capacity prewarm recommendations.
